questions.stem: All of the sensations are relayed in the spinal nucleus of trigeminal nerve except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Proprioception

Sensory Components of the Trigeminal Nerve

  • The sensations of pain, temperature, touch, and pressure from the skin of the face and mucous membranes travel along axons whose cell bodies are situated in the semilunar or trigeminal sensory ganglion.
  • The sensations of touch and pressure are conveyed by nerve fibers that terminate in the main sensory nucleus. The sensations of pain and temperature pass to the spinal nucleus.
  • Proprioceptive impulses from the muscles of mastication and from the facial and extraocular muscles are carried by fibers in the sensory root of the trigeminal nerve that have bypassed the semilunar or trigeminal ganglion. The fibers cells of origin are the unipolar cells of the mesencephalic nucleus.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1464.e12-1464.e15.

questions.stem: Spinal cord ends at which level in adults?
questions.solutionHtml:
L1

Spinal cord

  • The spinal cord occupies the superior two-thirds of the vertebral canal. It is continuous cranially with the medulla oblongata just below the level of the foramen magnum, at the upper border of the atlas. It terminates caudally as the conus medullaris.
  • During development, the vertebral column elongates more rapidly than the spinal cord, so that there is an increasing discrepancy between the anatomical level of spinal cord segments and their corresponding vertebrae.
  • In later fetal life, the conus medullaris lies between the third lumbar and fifth sacral vertebrae.
  • In premature and term neonates, it lies between the first and third lumbar vertebrae
  • In the adult, the spinal cord terminates on average at the level of the middle third of the body of the first lumbar vertebra which corresponds approximately to the trans pyloric plane.



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-425.

questions.stem: Where do the axons of Purkinje cells relay?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dentate nucleus
  • The Purkinje cells send an inhibitory output to the deep cerebellar nuclei (a small set of fibers go directly to the vestibular nuclei).
  • It is the balance of inhibitory signals from the Purkinje cells versus the excitatory signals from the climbing and mossy fiber collaterals that dictate the activity of the deep cerebellar nuclei.
  • The deep cerebellar nuclei are the final common pathway for signals leaving the cerebellum.



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-468-470.

questions.stem: Neurovascular bundle is absent in which of the following compartment of leg?
questions.solutionHtml:
Superficial posterior
  • There is no artery or motor nerve in the  superficial posterior compartment and the artery belonging to the lateral compartment actually resides in the deep posterior.
  • The deep posterior has TWO arteries (the posterior tibial and the peroneal), the lateral has none (but feeds off the peroneal). The anterior has the anterior tibial artery.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1398.

questions.stemHtml: Where does the marked structure arise from?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hippocampus

(Marked structure is FORNIX)

  • The fibers of fornix arise mainly from the pyramidal cells of the hippocampus and form a thin layer of white fibers on its ventricular surface called alveus.
  • The crus of fornix as it arches upwards, medially and forwards underneath the splenium of corpus callosum. The two crura, one of each hemisphere, curving over the thalamus, converge and unite in the midline beneath the trunk of corpus callosum to form the body of fornix. Anteriorly, the body of fornix divides into two columns. Each column of fornix arches downwards towards the anterior commissure, and forms the anterior boundary of interventricular foramen. Then it curves posteriorly through the hypothalamus to end in the mammillary body.

Fornix




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-538.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not seen in oculomotor nerve palsy?

options.label: C
options.text: Deviation of eyeball laterally and superiorly

questions.answerText: Deviation of eyeball laterally and superiorly
questions.solutionHtml:
Deviation of eyeball laterally and superiorly

The damage of oculomotor nerve clinically presents as:

  • Ptosis (drooping of the upper eyelid), due to paralysis of the levator palpebrae superioris
  • Lateral strabismus (i.e., lateral squint), due to paralysis of the medial rectus and consequent unopposed action of the lateral rectus muscle
  • Dilated and fixed pupil, due to paralysis of the sphincter pupillae and consequent unopposed action of the dilator pupillae.
  • Loss of accommodation, due to paralysis of the medial rectus, sphincter pupillae, and ciliaris muscles abducted the eye.
  • Double vision or diplopia occurs on looking medially, inferiorly, and superiorly, due to paralysis of the medial rectus, inferior rectus, and inferior oblique muscles
  • IO and MR involvement: eyeball moves inferiorly and laterally (“down and out”)

Oculomotor nerve Palsy




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1464.e11, 1464.e12.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a nucleus of upward gaze?
questions.solutionHtml:
Interstitial nucleus of Cajal
  • The three key structures in the control of the vertical gaze center include the rostral interstitial nucleus of the medial longitudinal fasciculus (riMLF), the interstitial nucleus of Cajal (INC), and the posterior commissure (PC). The riMLF is located in the midbrain and helps with vertical and torsional saccades.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-481.

questions.stem: Inferior thyroid artery is a branch of?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thyrocervical trunk

The inferior thyroid artery is an artery in the neck. It arises from the thyrocervical trunk and passes upward, in front of the vertebral artery and longus colli muscle.

Inferior thyroid artery




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1464.e86.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding the nerve supply of adrenal gland?

options.label: A
options.text: Preganglionic fibers from lower thoracic and lumbar vertebra come via sympathetic chain to supply adrenals

options.label: B
options.text: Adrenal medulla doesn’t have nerve supply

options.label: C
options.text: Adrenal cortex doesn’t have nerve supply as it has endocrine functions

options.label: D
options.text: Release of Catecholamines is not affected by nerve supply to adrenals

questions.answerText: Preganglionic fibers from lower thoracic and lumbar vertebra come via sympathetic chain to supply adrenals
questions.solutionHtml:
Preganglionic fibers from lower thoracic and lumbar vertebra come via sympathetic chain to supply adrenals
  • The adrenal glands are innervated by the coeliac plexus and greater splanchnic nerves. Sympathetic innervation to the adrenal medulla is via myelinated presynaptic fibres, mainly from the T10 to L1 spinal cord segments.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1464.e47.

questions.stem: Which of the following is false regarding blood supply of dura mater?

options.label: A
options.text: Meningeal branch of ICA in posterior cranial fossa

options.label: C
options.text: Meningeal branch of anterior and posterior ethmoidal artery supplies ACF

questions.answerText: Meningeal branch of ICA in posterior cranial fossa
questions.solutionHtml:
Meningeal branch of ICA in posterior cranial fossa
  • In the posterior fossa, the dura is supplied by the meningeal branches of the occipital artery (one enters the skull by the jugular-foramen and another by the mastoid foramen), the posterior meningeal branches of the vertebral artery, occasional small branches of the ascending pharyngeal artery, which enter by the jugular foramen and hypoglossal canal, and the dorsal meningeal and tentorial arteries arising from the meningo hypophyseal trunk.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-404.
